task_description: Build laya-browser-mcp: a TypeScript/Node 22 MCP server that is a superset of Playwright MCP plus a local sub-100ms Laya on-device decision engine. Assist mode (ref-based accessibility snapshot + familiar browser tools, works standalone with no weights) and Autopilot mode (laya_run_goal loop: snapshot -> typed page state -> local Laya narrow decision + deterministic rules -> Playwright execution -> repeat, with MCP-sampling escalation to the client LLM on low confidence/BLOCKED, degrading gracefully when weights are absent). Verified offline with a stubbed Laya and local HTML fixtures. Honest positioning: strong on structured forms, limited on arbitrary real sites; not a fully autonomous general web agent.

review.summary: v1 semantic review APPROVED (reviewer independently ran typecheck/build/tests and read every source/test file). Three non-blocking precision/documentation findings were then addressed in commit 886a23b: renamed the benchmark 'step accuracy' to honest 'expected-ops coverage', scoped the destructive-form guard to the target/neighbour controls (removed the whole-page visible-text false-positive), and clarified in the README that the guard covers the Autopilot auto-submit path only.

verification.summary: pnpm run typecheck + build clean. vitest: 51 passed, 2 skipped (real-weights integration tests gated behind LAYA_MODEL_DIR). pnpm run bench: 3/3 clean fixtures end-to-end via the INDEPENDENT final-page check, 100% per-step. Test quality reviewed: tests drive real headless Chromium and assert literal DOM outcomes (e.g. #results text, #status unchanged after a safety guard, source='llm' in the escalation transcript); a rogue DONE-only engine test proves DONE is not treated as success (verification.verified=false). Escalation uses the real SDK server.createMessage sampling API with capability probing and boundary-guarded parsing. No Dockerfile in the project, so docker_build is skipped.
